question: Why do green beans turn khaki when dressed in lemon juice or vinegar?
answer: Acid evicts a metal. Chlorophyll holds a magnesium atom at its centre; hydrogen ions from the acid knock it out, leaving olive-brown pheophytin. Heat speeds the swap, which is why cooks dress greens at the last moment. A pinch of bicarbonate keeps them bright, but alkali also dissolves their cell walls into mush.
move: Every fix has a side effect; ask what the improvement costs.
source: Belitz, Grosch and Schieberle, Food Chemistry, 2009
reference: Belitz, Grosch and Schieberle, Food Chemistry, 4th edition, Springer, 2009
